chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibrahim al-Kazzaz, Abu Ayub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who was unconscious for days and did not pray, then he regained consciousness. Does he pray what he missed? He said: There is nothing upon him.

key_terms.أَيَّاماً: For days / A period of days
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is nothing upon him / No obligation

ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up missed prayers if I was unconscious for several days?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of exemption from qada (making up) prayers for those who lose consciousness for an extended period, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the state of unconsciousness removes the obligation of prayer entirely during that time. Unlike the Hanafi school which often requires making up prayers after short periods of unconsciousness, this narration supports the view that the divine burden is lifted when the individual is not in a state of accountability. The ruling underscores the mercy in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring that temporary incapacitation does not result in an accumulating debt of worship.
